plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers on sturdy stems above broad, blue-green leaves. Thousands of cultivars exist, ranging from simple single blooms to frilly parrot and double forms. Peak bloom occurs in mid-spring across temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to early May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Netherlands, northern Europe, North America, and temperate gardens worldwide; native to Central Asia
plants.funFact: During the 17th-century 'Tulip Mania' in the Netherlands, single bulbs sold for more than the price of a luxurious canal house.

plants.name: Cornus florida
plants.description: A small deciduous tree whose showy display comes from four petal-like bracts surrounding a tight cluster of tiny greenish-yellow true flowers. The blooms appear before or as the leaves emerge, lighting up eastern woodlands and suburban yards.
plants.location: Eastern United States, from southern New England to Florida and west to Texas
plants.funFact: The bright red fruits that follow the flowers are an important autumn food source for songbirds, and the tree is the state tree of Virginia and Missouri.

plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: A vigorous woody climbing vine producing long, pendulous clusters of fragrant pea-like flowers. Blooms open all at once before the leaves fully expand, creating cascading curtains of color over pergolas, walls, and trees.
plants.location: Native to China; widely cultivated in Japan, Europe, and the southeastern United States
plants.funFact: Wisteria vines can live for over a century, and the twining stems can grow strong enough to crush wooden structures and drainpipes.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Not suited to April; replaced here by an autumn bloomer of the Southern Hemisphere. Nerine bowdenii, a bulbous perennial, sends up naked stems topped with umbels of narrow, wavy-petaled, sparkling flowers just as autumn begins in southern regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn in the Southern Hemisphere (March to May)
plants.location: Native to South Africa's Eastern Cape and Drakensberg; naturalized in parts of Australia and New Zealand
plants.funFact: The petals of Nerine have a crystalline surface that glitters in sunlight, which is why it is sometimes called the Guernsey lily or 'diamond lily'.
